Omission candidate review for the 66 Sol windows

632 accepted · 11 held for review · 163 rejected · 66 windows with at least one accepted omission

All existing omission-splitter units with deterministic punctuation-boundary repairs and independent full-window review by gpt-6-astra. Failed boundary repairs receive a fresh review of the original boundaries. Removed lexical content and doses are unchanged. No Chinese wording was written by hand. No QAs or prior decisions were sent to the reviewer. Each preview removes one highlighted span in isolation. Character counts exclude punctuation. Combining edits requires a new read of the window.

Accepted without flags: 267. Accepted with flags: 365 (included in the accepted total).

These are omission-splitter candidates. Word/phrase/clause size is classification only; narrow English alignment is supporting evidence, not an acceptance gate. The reviewer reads the full paired window. A concrete event need not be central to the entire story. Standalone markers and removals without substantive content remain ineligible.

Accepted unit classifications · clause: 594 · phrase: 35 · word: 3. Use these classifications, not the splitter label, for mixture accounting. Unit flags describe classification; they do not indicate a defective omission.

296 candidates have automatic punctuation-boundary repairs, retaining the same removed lexical content and character dose. Their original deletions are recorded below.

Original units selected in current passages: 192 accepted · 1 held for review · 34 rejected. This audit does not replace those passages or validate combinations of edits.

Changes from the earlier audit
  • Previously accepted: 297 accepted · 0 held for review · 1 rejected
  • Previously rejected: 335 accepted · 11 held for review · 162 rejected

Failed checks · fluent (84) · key content removed (81) · information omitted (60). One rejected candidate can fail more than one check.

Acceptance requires yes on all 5 checks — information omitted, fluent, deletion only, valid in context, key content removed. A no causes rejection; unresolved required-check uncertainty is held for review. Fluency requires natural, grammatical Chinese.

The omission treatment removes source information through deletion. Fluent omissions can be accepted with additional semantic distortion flags. These flags record secondary mistranslation effects without causing rejection. Possible other meaning changed records uncertainty about the secondary effect.

Flags on accepted omissions · recoverable from context (215) · ambiguous reference (122) · possible other meaning changed (76) · other meaning changed (47) · unit phrase (35) · unit word (3). A candidate can have several flags.

Accepted (632)
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · 耶罗波安站在祭坛旁烧香的时候， — The edited sentence naturally describes the man's arrival but no longer states that Jeroboam was standing beside the altar burning incense when it occurred.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · 有一个神人奉耶和华的话， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — The arrival remains, but its actor is no longer explicitly identified as a man of God acting by the LORD's word. Chinese permits an implicit subject here. However, the remaining named participant, Jeroboam, can now be understood as the person arriving; the later reference to 神人 supports a different contextual recovery.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · 他奉耶和华的话向祭坛呼喊说： (recoverable from context) — The direct quotation reads naturally after the man's introduction. Its address to the altar and claim of divine origin remain explicit, and the speaker is contextually recoverable. Nevertheless, the narration that he cried out by the LORD's word is removed; this is more than deletion of a generic 'said'.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · ，名叫约西亚 — The deletion removes the son's name, Josiah. The remaining prediction is grammatical, and the following 他 still clearly refers to the son.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · 他必在你上面， (recoverable from context · unit phrase) — Josiah remains a recoverable implicit subject, and the prophetic context supports the future reading of 将那些……献为祭. However, the sacrifice itself is no longer explicitly located on the addressed altar. The surviving 在你上面 inside the relative clause locates the priests' incense burning, not their sacrifice.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · 将那些在你上面烧香的丘坛祭司献为祭， (other meaning changed) — The entire prediction of sacrificing the incense-burning high-place priests disappears. The remainder is repetitive but grammatical: 他必在你上面 can stand as a locative predicate, followed by the bone-burning prediction. This also changes the original locative modifier of sacrificing into a standalone assertion that Josiah will be on the altar.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · ，也必在你上面焚烧人的骨头 — The deletion removes the separate prediction of burning human bones on the altar. The remaining sentence naturally ends with the prediction of sacrificing the priests.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · 当天， (recoverable from context · unit word) — The edit removes the explicit statement that the sign was given that same day. Narrative continuity suggests this timing, but no longer states it. The remaining Chinese is grammatical.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · 神人给了一个预兆， (recoverable from context) — The explicit narration that the man of God gave a sign disappears. The surviving quotation identifies a sign, but does not retain that explicit narrated action. In the full window, the previous speaking subject supplies the implicit subject of 当天，说, so the omission does not make the Chinese ungrammatical.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · 这是耶和华所说的预兆： (recoverable from context) — The edit removes the explicit assertion that the LORD spoke this sign. The earlier verses establish divine authorization generally, but the edited verse no longer explicitly attributes this particular sign to the LORD. The adjacent outer and inner quotation marks are redundant but do not make the sentence ungrammatical.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · 这祭坛必裂开， — The deletion removes the prediction that the altar will split apart. The remaining prediction about ashes spilling out is grammatical and does not itself state that the altar will split. The edited verse results from the exact deletion supplied.
  • 1 Kings 13:1–3 · ，坛上的灰必倾撒出来 — The deletion removes the prediction that the altar's ashes will be poured out. The retained prediction that the altar will split is natural Chinese and does not explicitly express the separate event involving the ashes. The supplied edit is deletion only.
  • 1 Kings 13:6–7 · 王就对神人说： (recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the explicit identification of the king as speaker and the man of God as his addressee. The opening direct quotation remains grammatical; its participants can be inferred from the ensuing intercession and restoration, and from verse 13:7.
  • 1 Kings 13:6–7 · 请你恳求耶和华你的神， (recoverable from context) — The remaining request naturally asks for prayer and restoration, but no longer specifies that the prayer should be directed to the LORD or describes him as the man of God's God. The subsequent narrative supplies the divine recipient, not the deleted explicit relationship.
  • 1 Kings 13:6–7 · ，使我的手恢复原状 (recoverable from context) — The edited request fluently asks for intercession and prayer but does not state the desired restoration of the king's hand. The later report of restoration makes that purpose inferable without retaining it explicitly in the request.
  • 1 Kings 13:6–7 · 于是神人恳求耶和华， — The exact deletion leaves grammatical Chinese but removes the actual performance of the intercession. The surviving request and healing do not themselves state that the man of God interceded.
  • 1 Kings 13:6–7 · 王的手就恢复了， (other meaning changed) — The restoration event disappears. The remaining construction “于是神人恳求耶和华，和从前一样” is grammatical with the comparison referring to the intercession, but this changes the comparison from the hand's restored condition to the man's praying as before. That additional distortion is nonblocking.
  • 1 Kings 13:6–7 · 王对神人说： (recoverable from context) — The standalone quotation is natural after 13:6. Its speaker and addressee can be inferred from the preceding exchange, but the edited statement no longer explicitly attributes this invitation and promise to the king speaking to the man of God.
  • 1 Kings 13:6–7 · 请跟我回家， — 删除准确移除了随王回家的邀请；余文“吃喝休息一下，我必给你赏赐”自然完整，仍保留休息邀请和赏赐承诺，但不再表达同行回家。
  • 1 Kings 13:6–7 · 吃喝休息一下， — 删除准确移除了吃喝休息的邀请。“请跟我回家，我必给你赏赐”语法自然；回家邀请本身并未明确表达让神人休息恢复精神。
  • 1 Kings 13:6–7 · ，我必给你赏赐 — 删除准确移除了王给予赏赐的承诺；余文“请跟我回家，吃喝休息一下”仍是自然完整的邀请，未再说明王将给予赏赐。
  • 1 Kings 13:8–10 · 神人却回答： (recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the explicit identification of the speaker as the man of God and the statement that he is replying. The remaining direct quotation is grammatical without an introductory speech clause. Verse 13:10 helps recover the speaker, but does not preserve explicit attribution of this speech.
  • 1 Kings 13:8–10 · 你就是把一半的财产给我， — The edited verse omits the concrete hypothetical offer of half the addressee's possessions. The remaining refusal is natural Chinese; 也 can function as an additive particle without requiring the deleted 就是 clause.
  • 1 Kings 13:8–10 · 我也不会跟你去， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — The refusal to accompany the addressee disappears. The remaining main clause can naturally have an implicit first-person subject, recoverable from 给我 and the speaker's explanation in 13:9. However, without 我, 也不会在这地方吃饭喝水 can also be read as continuing the subject 你, potentially shifting who will not eat or drink.
  • 1 Kings 13:8–10 · ，也不会在这地方吃饭喝水 (recoverable from context) — The edited verse retains the conditional refusal to accompany the addressee but removes the separate refusal to eat or drink in that place. The resulting sentence is grammatical. Verse 13:9 supplies the underlying prohibition, but that does not explicitly retain this declaration of refusal.
  • 1 Kings 13:8–10 · 因为耶和华的话这样吩咐我： (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — 删除后，禁令本身仍是完整、合乎语法的引语，但不再说明这是耶和华借自己的话向神人发出的命令，也不再明确把该命令作为前节拒绝的原因。内层引语中的“你”失去明确的受命者说明，可能被理解为神人对当前听者说的话，而非神人引用自己收到的命令。
  • 1 Kings 13:8–10 · 你不可吃饭， (recoverable from context) — 删除了不得吃饭这一独立禁令。剩余的“不可喝水，也不可沿原路返回”可以自然省略主语，受命者由“吩咐我”提供。13:8仍提到拒绝吃饭，但不能替代本节明确陈述吃饭受到禁止。
  • 1 Kings 13:8–10 · 不可喝水， (recoverable from context) — 删除了不可喝水这一独立禁令，剩余的“你不可吃饭，也不可沿原路返回”语法自然。13:8的拒绝喝水仍然存在，但本节不再明确把喝水列为耶和华禁止的行为。
  • 1 Kings 13:8–10 · ，也不可沿原路返回 — 删除了不可沿来路返回这一独立禁令，剩余两项饮食禁令构成自然完整的引语。13:10仍叙述神人实际另走一条路，但实际行动不能保留本节被删除的路线禁令。
  • 1 Kings 13:8–10 · 于是神人走了另一条路， (recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the affirmative action of taking another route. The remaining negative statement says that the man did not return along his incoming route, without explicitly reporting the alternative-route action. Its implicit subject is naturally recoverable as the man of God from the preceding dialogue.
  • 1 Kings 13:8–10 · ，没有沿着来伯特利的原路返回 (recoverable from context) — The remaining sentence is grammatical and reports taking another route. The deletion removes the explicit identification of the avoided route as the one used to come to Bethel, including the named destination. Avoidance of the incoming route remains inferable from the command and the surviving action, but the Bethel detail is no longer stated.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 伯特利住着一个老先知。 (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the introduction of an old prophet residing in Bethel. The remaining Chinese is grammatical, although the opening 他 lacks an immediately established antecedent. The subsequent references to 父亲 and 先知 help identify him, but do not restore his residence or age.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 他的儿子们来， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The sons' coming is a distinct action and disappears even though their subsequent reporting remains. The reporting clauses now have an implicit subject; the reference to 父亲 and the following verse's explicit 儿子们 allow that subject to be recovered. This makes the transition less explicit, but does not require judging the Chinese ungrammatical.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 把神人当天在伯特利所做的一切事都告诉了他， — The edited verse retains the sons' arrival and their report of the words spoken to the king, but removes their report of the deeds. The remaining sequence “他的儿子们来，也把……告诉了父亲” is grammatical; 也 can add the reporting action to their coming.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · ，也把神人对王说的话告诉了父亲 — Accepted. The edited verse naturally reports the sons' account of the deeds but no longer states that they also relayed the man's words to the king.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 父亲问他们： (recoverable from context) — Accepted. The unattributed question is natural in this narrative context, but the explicit statement that the father asked his sons is removed. The surrounding exchange makes that attribution recoverable rather than explicit.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 儿子们就把那位从犹大来的神人所走的路指给他看。 (recoverable from context) — Accepted. The remaining question connects naturally to the subsequent donkey preparations, but the sons' act of showing the route is no longer stated. The deleted identification of the man as coming from Judah is repeated in 13:14.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 于是先知对儿子们说： (recoverable from context) — The command remains natural as unattributed dialogue following the father–sons exchange. However, the edited statement no longer explicitly identifies the prophet as its speaker or his sons as its recipients; these roles are recoverable from the surrounding narrative.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 他们就为他备好驴， — The edited narrative naturally moves from the command to the prophet mounting and pursuing the man of God. It no longer states that the sons actually saddled the donkey for him; mounting the donkey does not preserve that distinct action.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 他便骑上， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — The prophet's mounting disappears. Across the verse boundary, “他们就为他备好驴，去追赶神人” is grammatical, but its default subject continuity can make the sons, rather than the prophet, the pursuers. The broader narrative allows the intended prophet referent to be inferred, so this is a possible additional meaning change rather than a fluency failure.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 去追赶神人。 — The deletion removes the prophet's pursuit of the man of God. Finding him afterward does not explicitly preserve that distinct action. The preceding mounting clause and the remaining finding clause form a grammatical narrative sequence.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 他找到神人， (recoverable from context) — The explicit statement that the prophet found the man of God disappears. His subsequently seeing and questioning him makes the successful encounter recoverable, but no longer explicitly states the finding. The subject of “看见……就问” is naturally supplied by the preceding pursuit narrative.
  • 1 Kings 13:11–14 · 看见他正坐在一棵橡树下， — The edited verse naturally proceeds from finding the man to questioning him, but no longer states that he was sitting under an oak tree.
  • 1 Kings 13:20–22 · 他们坐席的时候， — The deletion removes the circumstance that they were sitting at the table when the revelation came. The remaining Chinese is a complete, natural sentence, and the edit consists solely of the specified deletion.
  • 1 Kings 13:20–22 · 耶和华的话临到那位带神人回来的先知。 — 删去了耶和华的话临到先知这一事件，以及该先知曾带神人回来的身份说明。余下的“他们坐席的时候，”可自然连接下一节“先知就向……呼喊说”，在完整窗口中语法成立。
  • 1 Kings 13:20–22 · 先知就向那位从犹大来的神人呼喊说： (recoverable from context) — The remaining direct quotation reads naturally after the revelation in 13:20 and continues into 13:22. The prophet's role can be inferred, but his crying out to the man of God and that man's origin in Judah are no longer explicitly stated. This is more than redundant speech framing.
  • 1 Kings 13:20–22 · 耶和华如此说： (recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the explicit attribution of the quoted declaration to the LORD within 13:21. Its divine source remains recoverable from 13:20, but the edited reporting clause explicitly names only the prophet as speaker. The adjacent opening quotation marks retain a nested quotation; they do not make the continuing Chinese sentence ungrammatical.
  • 1 Kings 13:20–22 · 因为你违背了耶和华的话， (recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the explicit accusation of defying the LORD's word and the explicit causal introduction linking the offenses to the burial consequence. Related disobedience remains stated, so much of the accusation is recoverable. The remaining Chinese is grammatical: the addressed person can remain the implicit subject of “没有遵守” and the following actions.
  • 1 Kings 13:20–22 · 没有遵守耶和华你的神给你的命令， (recoverable from context) — The edited proclamation still accuses the man of defiance, but no longer explicitly says that he failed to keep a command given to him by the LORD his God. Verse 13:22 preserves a particular prohibition and its violation, making some of this information recoverable. The causal sentence remains grammatical across the verse boundary.
  • 1 Kings 13:20–22 · 反而回去， (recoverable from context) — The return journey disappears from the accusation, while eating and drinking remain. Returning is a distinct action, not simply another expression of consuming food and water. The earlier description of the prophet bringing him back makes the return recoverable. The remaining locative action clause connects naturally to 13:21.
  • 1 Kings 13:20–22 · 在他吩咐你不可吃饭喝水的地方吃了饭、喝了水， — The deletion removes the specific eating and drinking offenses and the prohibition attached to their location. The remaining sentence naturally continues the causal accusation in 13:21 with “反而回去” and then announces the burial consequence. It retains general disobedience but no longer specifies these violations.
  • 1 Kings 13:23–25 · 神人吃喝完毕， (ambiguous reference) — The deletion removes the completion of eating and drinking before the donkey was prepared, as well as the explicit identification of the traveler as the man of God. The remaining Chinese is grammatical, although 他 no longer has an explicitly identified antecedent within this window.
  • 1 Kings 13:23–25 · ，那位带他回来的老先知就为他备好驴 — 神人吃喝完毕。 is a complete, natural sentence. The deletion removes the old prophet's preparation of the donkey for the traveler and the statement that this prophet had brought him back. The later appearance of the donkey does not state its preparation.
  • 1 Kings 13:23–25 · 他上路后， (recoverable from context) — The edited verse remains natural and retains the roadside encounter and killing. It no longer explicitly states that the traveler had set out before the encounter. His presence on the road makes that action inferable but does not explicitly express it.
  • 1 Kings 13:23–25 · ，将他咬死 — The edit deletes exactly the specified span and leaves grammatical Chinese. It retains the encounter and the man's subsequent corpse, but no longer explicitly states that the lion killed him. The surviving outcome does not preserve the distinct killing action.
  • 1 Kings 13:23–25 · 他的尸体倒在路上， (recoverable from context) — The exact deletion leaves a natural transition from the killing to the animals standing beside the corpse. The corpse is readily identifiable from the preceding death, but its lying in the road is no longer explicitly asserted in this verse. That detail is repeated in 13:25.
  • 1 Kings 13:23–25 · ，驴和狮子都站在尸体旁边 (recoverable from context) — The edit is an exact deletion and leaves two complete, natural sentences. It removes the statement that both animals stood beside the corpse. The next verse restores the lion's position, but not the donkey's.
  • 1 Kings 13:23–25 · 有人经过， (ambiguous reference) — The exact deletion removes the introduction of people passing by and their passing action. The remaining observation-and-report sequence permits an implicit human subject in Chinese and is grammatical, although those observers are now less explicitly anchored. Seeing and reporting do not themselves state that the observers were passing by.
  • 1 Kings 13:23–25 · 看见尸体倒在路上， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — 删除后不再明说路人看见倒在路上的尸体。中文仍可按场景插述理解，让“就到……报告”的省略主语承接“有人”，但中间出现“狮子”使主语承接有歧义，也可能误读为狮子去报告。尸体所在位置可由13:24恢复，路人的看见行为则不再明确表达。
  • 1 Kings 13:23–25 · 狮子站在尸体旁边， (recoverable from context) — 编辑句自然地叙述路人经过、看见尸体并前去报告，但不再交代他们所见情景中有狮子站在尸体旁边。13:24虽已记载狮子的位置，也不能替代本句被删除的明确陈述。
  • 1 Kings 13:23–25 · ，就到老先知所住的城里报告了这件事 — 编辑句仍自然地描述路人看见尸体及旁边的狮子，但完全删除了路人前往老先知居住的城并报告此事的后续行动。删除内容由13:25英文直接支持。
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 那位把神人从路上带回来的先知听见了， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the prophet's hearing the report and his identification as the person who brought the man of God back. The remaining 就说 permits an implicit subject in Chinese; the old prophet in the following verse helps identify the speaker, although the attribution is less explicit.
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 这是那违背耶和华命令的神人。 — The edit removes the identification of the victim as the disobedient man of God, including the stated reason for the judgment. The remaining quotation is grammatical. 因此 now invokes an unstated reason, but that discourse gap does not make the Chinese ungrammatical; 他 can refer to 神人 in the introductory clause.
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 耶和华将他交给狮子， — The edited quotation naturally connects disobedience with the lion's attack, but no longer states that the LORD actively delivered the man to the lion. The surviving attack and fulfillment of the LORD's words do not preserve that distinct action.
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 狮子就撕咬他， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — 删除了狮子撕咬神人的动作；保留咬死的结果并不等于明确保留这一动作。剩余句可按语境补出“将他咬死”的主语为狮子，语法成立，但也可能顺接前面的主语“耶和华”，造成施事歧义。
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 将他咬死， (recoverable from context) — 编辑后的句子自然，但仅说狮子撕咬神人，不再明确说狮子将他咬死。后文的尸体和安葬可帮助恢复死亡信息，不抵消本句死亡结果的删除。
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · ，正如耶和华对他所说的话 — 编辑后保留了交给狮子、撕咬及死亡，句子自然完整；但不再陈述这些事件符合耶和华先前对神人所说的话。这是实质性的对应关系，而非单纯话语标记。
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 老先知就吩咐儿子们： (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — 独立引语后接“他们便备好了驴”可以自然成句。前文有助于恢复说话者是先知，但编辑后不再明确说明受命并备驴的是他的儿子们；“他们”的具体身份因而不明。删除不只是冗余引语框架。
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 他们便备好了驴。 — 余文是完整自然的命令叙述，但不再陈述儿子们已经执行命令、备好了驴。命令仍在并不等于执行事件仍被表达。
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 他去了， — 删除后不再明确叙述老先知前往现场的行动，只保留找到尸体及现场情况。“找到那倒在路上的尸体”的隐含主语可由前文老先知及其备驴要求理解，在连续叙事中可以成立。
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 找到那倒在路上的尸体， — 余文“他去了，驴和狮子都站在尸体旁边”能够自然衔接前往行动与现场描写，尸体也可由前文神人被咬死理解。但老先知找到尸体的事件，以及尸体倒在路上的具体位置和状态，均不再明确陈述。
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · ，驴和狮子都站在尸体旁边 — 删除后不再说明驴和狮子都站在尸体旁边。找到尸体及狮子未吃尸体、未撕咬驴的叙述仍然完整自然；这两项否定并不表达动物当时的位置。
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 狮子既没有吃尸体， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — 狮子没有吃尸体这一事实被删除。“也没有撕咬驴”可作为承接前文的省略主语句，结合上下文可理解为狮子没有撕咬驴，不能仅因主语省略判为语病。不过，前一句的显式主语是“驴和狮子”，因此剩余否定句也可能被读成承接这个并列主语，而非仅指狮子。
  • 1 Kings 13:26–30 · 老先知就抬起神人的尸体， (recoverable from context) — 编辑后仍可结合前文理解为老先知把尸体放在驴背上并运回安葬，主语和宾语的省略符合中文连续叙事的用法。但“抬起”尸体这一独立动作已不再明确叙述，不能因后续放置、运输动作仍在而认定信息完全保留。

It no longer states her subsequent action against all royal heirs. The next verse supplies related evidence of royal sons being murdered, but does not explicitly restore Athaliah's undertaking or its comprehensive scope.
  • 2 Kings 11:1–3 · 但约兰王的女儿、亚哈谢的姐妹约示巴， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed · unit phrase) — The remaining 将 construction can grammatically have an implicit subject, so the absence of an explicit subject is not itself a fluency failure. However, Jehosheba and both of her family relationships disappear. Because Athaliah is the preceding female actor, the omitted subject and subsequent 她 could now be read as Athaliah, incorrectly attributing the rescue to her.

Their escape and Joash’s survival do not explicitly preserve that action or location. The remaining “躲避亚他利雅，使他没有被杀。” can naturally continue the rescue narrative with an implicit subject. The nurse’s subsequent presence is recoverable from 11:3, but the bedroom concealment is not.
  • 2 Kings 11:1–3 · 躲避亚他利雅， (recoverable from context) — The edited sentence remains grammatical and retains the concealment and survival outcome, but no longer explicitly identifies Athaliah as the person from whom Joash was hidden. Her role as the threat is inferable from 11:1 rather than stated in the edited rescue account.

It no longer explicitly states the successful outcome that Joash was not killed. His continued life is inferable from the six years of hiding in 11:3, but that does not preserve the explicit outcome in the edited statement.

The remaining Chinese permits an implicit subject, but 他 and 他们 no longer have explicitly introduced referents in the displayed window. This referential ambiguity does not itself make the construction ungrammatical.

  • 2 Kings 11:4–8 · 三分之一要守在苏珥门， — The instruction to station one third at the gate of Sur is removed. The palace assignment in 11:5 joins naturally to the surviving assignment at the gate behind the guards; the shortened list remains grammatical.

  • 2 Kings 7:1–2 · 你们要听耶和华的话！ — Accepted. The edited verse naturally introduces the LORD’s prediction but no longer commands the audience to hear the LORD’s word.
  • 2 Kings 7:1–2 · 明天约在这时候， (unit phrase) — Accepted. The remaining prediction is fluent and retains its location, commodities, quantities, and prices, but loses the specified time of fulfillment.
  • 2 Kings 7:1–2 · 在撒马利亚城门口， (unit phrase) — The exact deletion removes the predicted sale location while leaving a natural statement of the time, commodities, quantities, and prices.
  • 2 Kings 7:1–2 · ，两细亚大麦也要卖一舍客勒银子 — The deletion removes the barley-price prediction. The remaining flour-price prediction is complete, natural, and supported by the source.
  • 2 Kings 7:1–2 · 那位供王扶着手臂的军官回答上帝的人说： (ambiguous reference) — The opening quotation remains grammatical without an explicit speech introduction, and Elisha’s subsequent reply makes the exchange intelligible. However, the challenger is no longer identified as the officer on whose arm the king leaned, leaving the speaker unidentified.
  • 2 Kings 7:1–2 · 就算耶和华在天上开了窗户， — The deletion removes the officer’s explicit hypothetical concession about the LORD making windows in heaven. The remaining question naturally refers to the prediction in 7:1 and remains grammatical.
  • 2 Kings 7:1–2 · 以利沙回答： (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the explicit identification of Elisha as the speaker of the response. Consecutive unattributed dialogue quotations can be grammatical Chinese, and the exchange makes Elisha’s role inferable, but the edited statement no longer expressly attributes the second quotation to him.
  • 2 Kings 7:1–2 · 你必亲眼看见， — 删除后不再明说军官将亲眼见证预言实现。“却一点也吃不到。”可承接窗口中粮食将供应充足的预言形成转折，省略的主语也可从以利沙正在回答军官的语境中确定，因此不构成语法错误。所示修改仅删除指定文字。
  • 2 Kings 7:1–2 · ，却一点也吃不到 — 删除后仅保留军官将亲眼看见的预告，不再陈述他无法吃到粮食。“你必亲眼看见。”在回应军官的疑问时自然完整，所见之事由前文预言提供。所示修改仅删除指定文字。
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · 城门入口处有四个患麻风病的人。 (ambiguous reference) — The deletion removes the introduction identifying the speakers, their number, their illness, and their location. “当时，他们彼此说” is grammatical, although “他们” no longer has an explicit antecedent in the displayed window.
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · 他们彼此说： (recoverable from context) — 人物介绍后直接接引语，在中文叙事中可以自然成立，且说话者仍可由上下文推知。不过，“彼此”明确表达的相互交谈关系不再明说，因此不只是删除冗余的泛泛引语框架。
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · 我们为什么坐在这里等死呢？ (recoverable from context) — 7:3留下的开引号可直接引出7:4的“如果我们说……”，整段对话仍自然完整。删除的是他们对继续坐着等死的明确反问；7:4仍保留坐着会死的后果和前往亚兰营地的提议，但没有保留这句反问本身。
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · 如果我们说： (other meaning changed) — 删除了把进城提议设为假设选项的条件框架。剩余文字语法成立，但“进城去吧”由假设中的提议变成直接发出的提议，与后面的死亡判断形成语意上的转折或冲突。
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · ‘进城去吧’， (other meaning changed) — The proposal to enter the city disappears. The remaining Chinese permits a grammatical reading in which “城里有饥荒” supplies the content of “我们说,” followed by the predicted death. This changes the conditional setup from proposing entry to speaking about the famine.
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · 城里有饥荒， — 编辑后条件句完整自然，仍说明进城会死亡，但不再交代城中饥荒及其作为死亡原因的信息。
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · 我们必死在那里； (recoverable from context) — 编辑后可自然理解为连续权衡两个选项：进城则面临城中饥荒，留在这里也会死。城中饥荒仍是对进城选项的回应，但进城必死这一明确结果已被删除；后面的“也必死”只能帮助推知该结果，不能替代其明说。
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · 如果坐在这里， (other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes remaining seated here as the condition for the second prediction of death. The remaining Chinese is grammatical, although repetitive. Without that condition, “我们也必死” reads as an unqualified prediction rather than the consequence of staying here. Verse 7:3 makes the omitted scenario recoverable.
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · 我们也必死。 (other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — The explicit prediction of death if they remain seated is removed. “如果坐在这里，来吧，我们到亚兰人的营地去” can grammatically function as a condition followed by an exhortation, although it now makes remaining there the circumstance for the exhortation rather than a condition leading to death. Verse 7:3 still suggests that staying means waiting for death.
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · ，我们到亚兰人的营地去 (ambiguous reference) — The deletion removes the proposal to go to the Aramean camp and the identification of the people encountered there. “来吧。” remains a grammatical exhortation, and the following conditional sentences are grammatical, but “他们” now lacks an explicit antecedent in the displayed window.
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · 他们若让我们活， (other meaning changed) — The deletion removes the condition that the Arameans permit the men to live. The remaining Chinese is grammatical: “我们就活” can connect to the preceding proposal to visit their camp. That connection changes conditional survival into an apparent consequence of going there.
  • 2 Kings 7:3–4 · 他们若杀我们， (other meaning changed) — The deletion removes the possible act of the Arameans killing the men and its role as the condition for death. The remaining clauses are grammatically complete, but “我们就死” now states death without its original condition, producing a changed and contextually discordant relationship to the preceding survival statement.
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · 那几个患麻风病的人到了营地边缘， (ambiguous reference) — 删除后不再交代行动者是患麻风病的人，也不再叙述他们到达营地边缘。开头的“进入一顶帐篷，又吃又喝”可以使用隐含主语，后文“他们”承接这一群行动者，因此不构成语法错误；但完整窗口内已无法确定他们的具体身份。
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · 进入一顶帐篷， (recoverable from context) — 编辑后的句子自然地叙述他们到达营地边缘并吃喝，但没有明确叙述进入第一顶帐篷这一动作。后文“又进了另一顶帐篷”可使读者推知先前的帐篷经历，却不能使被删除的事件仍然算作明确陈述。
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · ，又吃又喝 — 删除后仍自然地叙述到达、进入帐篷和拿取物品，但吃喝这一独立活动完全消失。英文明确支持该活动，且窗口其他位置没有重述。
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · 他们拿走银子、金子和衣服， (possible other meaning changed) — 删除后不再叙述第一次拿走物品的动作，也不再列出银子、金子和衣服。“随后，去藏了起来”可以承接前文人物作隐含主语，语法可成立。但失去物品先行项后，它更容易被理解为这些人自己躲藏起来，而原文说的是藏起拿走的物品。
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · ，去藏了起来 (recoverable from context) — Accepted. The edit removes the explicit action of going away and hiding the first batch of valuables. The remaining sentences are grammatical; “回来后” and the later “也藏了起来” leave that earlier activity partly inferable, not explicitly stated.
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · 回来后， — Accepted. Removing “回来后” deletes the explicit return event and its temporal relationship to entering the second tent. The remaining transition from hiding valuables to entering another tent is natural Chinese.
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · 他们又进了另一顶帐篷， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — Accepted. The edit removes entry into a distinct second tent. “回来后，从那里拿走一些东西，也藏了起来” permits the previously established people as its implicit subject and remains grammatical. However, “那里” no longer has the second tent as its explicit antecedent and may instead suggest the first tent or the camp.
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · 从那里拿走一些东西， (possible other meaning changed) — Accepted. Taking additional items from the second tent is no longer stated. The remaining “他们又进了另一顶帐篷，也藏了起来” is grammatical, but can now mean that the people themselves hid, rather than that they hid newly taken items.
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · ，也藏了起来 — The exact deletion leaves a natural sentence but removes the distinct action of hiding the items taken from the second tent. The earlier hiding event concerns the first tent's valuables and does not state this second event.
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · 我们这样做不对。 — The remaining quotation is natural and coherent. It no longer explicitly states their judgment that their present conduct is wrong; the later conditional warning about sin is not the same assertion.
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · 今天是个有好消息的日子。 — The exact deletion leaves fluent speech but removes the explicit characterization of today as a day of good news. The surviving proposal to report news does not explicitly preserve its favorable character or this statement about today.
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · 如果我们不作声， (other meaning changed) — The deletion removes remaining silent as a condition for the threatened consequence. The resulting Chinese is grammatical, but it presents the consequence at daybreak as unconditional rather than conditional on their silence and delay.
  • 2 Kings 7:8–9 · 等到天亮， — The edited conditional sentence is natural Chinese. It retains silence and the threatened consequence but no longer specifies waiting until morning.
  • 2 Kings 7:10–11 · 于是他们去向城门的守卫呼喊， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — 删后仍可作为省略主语的直接引语引入句，语法成立；但不再明说这些人前去向城门守卫呼喊报告。下一节守门人传报消息可以帮助推知接收者，却不能保留这一行动的明确陈述。
  • 2 Kings 7:10–11 · 我们到了亚兰人的营地， (ambiguous reference) — 删后引语在语法上自然，但“那里”在所给窗口中失去明确的地点先行词。原文明说他们到过亚兰人的营地，这一行动和具名地点均不再明确出现。
  • 2 Kings 7:10–11 · 只有拴着的马和驴， — 删除准确且余句自然。删去了营地仍有拴着的马和驴这一具体发现；无人和帐篷完好的陈述均不能表达该事实。
  • 2 Kings 7:10–11 · ，帐篷也都完好无损 — 删除准确，余句可自然结束于“只有拴着的马和驴”。帐篷仍完好无损这一独立观察不再出现，且窗口其他位置未补述。
  • 2 Kings 7:10–11 · 守门的人高声传报这消息， — 删除准确。“消息便传到了王宫”承接上一节的报告，自然且指代清楚。消息抵达王宫的结果虽保留，守门人高声传报这一独立行动及其施事者已不再明确陈述。
  • 2 Kings 7:10–11 · ，消息便传到了王宫 — 删除后只保留守门人高声传报消息的行动，不再说明消息传到了王宫。剩余句子“守门的人高声传报这消息。”自然完整，“这消息”由7:10提供明确指代。该编辑是纯删除，且所删结果有英文直接支持。
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 王夜里起来， (ambiguous reference) — The deletion removes the king's identification and his getting up at night. The remaining Chinese permits an implicit speaking subject, although the displayed edited window no longer identifies that speaker as the king.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 对臣仆们说： (recoverable from context) — The direct quotation can naturally follow the king's action without an explicit speech verb. However, the edited statement no longer explicitly identifies the servants as his audience. The servant's reply in 7:13 helps recover that relationship.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 让我告诉你们亚兰人对我们用了什么计策。 (ambiguous reference) — The remaining quotation is grammatical, but its opening 他们 no longer has an explicit Aramean antecedent in the displayed window. The deletion removes the named opposing group, not just the introductory announcement that the king will explain something.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 他们知道我们正挨饿， — The deletion removes the king's assertion that the Arameans know his people are starving, including the stated motivation for leaving camp. The remainder permits the Arameans as an implicit subject; 就离开营地 can introduce the described maneuver after the announcement of their stratagem, although the original explicit causal connection is gone.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 就离开营地， — The deletion removes the king's claim that the Arameans left their camp. Their hiding in the field remains, but that does not explicitly state the distinct departure action. The remaining predicates naturally share the subject 他们.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 藏在田野里， — The edited verse retains departure from the camp and the imagined capture plan, but removes the claim that the Arameans hide in the field. 就离开营地，心想 remains a natural sequence of predicates.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 等他们出城， — The deletion removes the condition that the Israelites first come out of the city. The remaining 我们就活捉他们，再进城去 is grammatical: 就 can introduce the planned next action without an explicit 等 clause.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 我们就活捉他们， — The exact deletion removes the planned capture of the people leaving the city. The remaining “等他们出城，再进城去” is grammatical: the understood subject of entering is the Arameans whose thoughts the king is describing.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · ，再进城去 — The exact deletion removes the intention to enter the city after capturing its inhabitants. The remaining conditional statement about capturing them alive is complete and natural.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 有一个臣仆回答说： (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — The exact deletion leaves a grammatical direct quotation but removes its attribution to one of the king's servants and its identification as a reply. Following the king's speech, the unattributed quotation could be mistaken for a continuation by the king; that attribution risk does not make the Chinese ungrammatical.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 请派侦察的人， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — The exact deletion removes the explicit instruction to dispatch scouts. The remaining imperative about taking five horses is grammatical with an implicit subject, and the final sentence still proposes sending people to investigate. Nevertheless, their explicit identification as scouts is lost, “他们” has a less secure antecedent, and the opening imperative can now sound like a direct instruction to the listener rather than an instruction to commission scouts.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · ，从城里剩下的马中带上五匹去吧 — Accepted. The exact deletion leaves the natural instruction “请派侦察的人” but removes the instruction to take five of the horses remaining in the city.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 他们的处境不会比留在这里的所有以色列人更糟。 — Accepted. The edited verse remains grammatical but no longer explicitly compares the scouts' plight with that of the Israelites staying in the city. The surviving statement that the Israelites are doomed does not express that comparison.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · ，这里所有的以色列人都难逃一死 (ambiguous reference) — Accepted. The explicit prediction of death for all the Israelites there disappears. “你也看到了。” can naturally stand with an implicit object referring to the preceding discussion of their plight, although its reference becomes less specific. Neither that expression nor the surviving comparison explicitly states that everyone there is doomed.
  • 2 Kings 7:12–13 · 就让我们派他们去探个究竟吧。 (recoverable from context) — Accepted: the deletion removes the explicit proposal to send the scouts to find out what has happened. The earlier request to dispatch scouts remains, but it does not explicitly state this investigative purpose. The edited speech is grammatical and ends naturally with the assessment that the Israelites face death.
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · 于是侦察的人带了两辆马车， (recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the scouts' taking two horse-drawn chariots. The remaining sentence is grammatical; the identity of “他们” can be recovered from the scouts mentioned in 7:15, but their taking the chariots cannot.
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · 王派他们去追踪亚兰军队， (other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — The king's dispatching the scouts after the Aramean army disappears. The remaining Chinese is grammatical, but “说” now naturally takes the scouts as its subject, changing the speaker of the command from the king to the scouts. Their pursuit remains recoverable from 7:15; the king's authorization does not.
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · 他们一路追踪， (possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — 删除后不再明确叙述侦察者实际一路追踪的行动；上一节派他们追踪的命令只能帮助推知该行动。余文“直到约旦河，果然沿途到处都是……”可以作为沿途景象的空间范围表达，语法可成立，但约旦河可能由追踪终点转而成为散落物分布的范围。
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · 直到约旦河， (unit phrase) — 删除后追踪行动及沿途所见仍然明确，句子自然，但追踪到约旦河这一具体地理终点消失。
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · ，果然沿途到处都是亚兰人匆忙逃跑时丢弃的衣服和装备 — 余文完整、自然地叙述追踪和返回报告，但删去了沿途散落物的发现，以及亚兰人仓促丢弃这些物品的事件。
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · 侦察的人就回来向王报告。 — 删除整句后，沿途所见的叙述仍完整，并可自然衔接下一节。但侦察者返回以及向王报告这两个行动均不再明说；下一节百姓出城抢掠不能替代这些事件。
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · 于是百姓出城， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — 删除确实移除了百姓出城这一事件及抢掠者的明确身份。剩余的“抢掠亚兰人的营地。”可以作为省略主语的叙事句，语法成立，但承接上文时可能被理解为侦察的人抢掠，而不是百姓抢掠。
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · ，抢掠亚兰人的营地 — 编辑后“于是百姓出城。”自然完整，但不再叙述百姓抢掠亚兰营地。后续粮价变化不能替代这一独立行动。
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · 一细亚细面卖一舍客勒银子， (ambiguous reference) — 删除后不再明确交代细面的数量及售价。剩余大麦价格句语法成立；“也”的比较对象变得不明确，但这种语境依赖不使句子不合语法，也不能恢复被删除的细面价格。
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · 两细亚大麦也卖一舍客勒银子， — Accepted: the exact deletion removes the independently stated barley price. The remaining Chinese naturally reports the plundering and flour price, with the concluding fulfillment statement still grammatical.
  • 2 Kings 7:14–16 · ，正如耶和华所说的 — Accepted: the exact deletion leaves a grammatical report of both prices but removes the explicit assertion that these outcomes accorded with the LORD's word.
  • 2 Kings 7:17–18 · 王先前派那位供他扶着手臂的军官负责看守城门， (ambiguous reference) — 删除后不再交代王任命军官看守城门，也失去死者的身份说明。剩余句子语法自然，但“把他踩死了”的“他”在所显示窗口中没有明确先行词；这是指称不明，而非语法错误。
  • 2 Kings 7:17–18 · 百姓却在城门口把他踩死了， (other meaning changed) — 删除明确移除了百姓踩死军官的事件，剩余中文自然且为纯删除。但“正如……所预言的”现在接在任命看守城门之后，使预言的对应事件由军官之死转为任命；这一附带意义变化单独标记。
  • 2 Kings 7:17–18 · ，正如上帝的人在王来见他时所预言的 — 剩余句子完整叙述任命和踩死事件，但不再明确说明军官之死应验了上帝的人的预言，也不再交代预言是在王来见他时作出的。7:18对粮价预言应验的叙述不能替代这些具体信息。
  • 2 Kings 7:17–18 · 事情果然照着上帝的人对王所说的发生了： (recoverable from context) — 独立引语在前文预言叙述之后可以自然成立，发言者也可由上下文推知。但删除的不只是引语框架：“事情……发生了”明确断言粮价预言已经应验，剩余的未来时引语不再表达这一结果，也不再明确标注该话是对王说的。
  • 2 Kings 7:17–18 · 明天约在这时候， (unit phrase) — 删除准确移除了预言实现的时间限定，余下的地点与两项售价陈述自然、完整；英文明确支持被删内容。
  • 2 Kings 7:17–18 · 在撒马利亚城门口， (unit phrase) — 删除准确移除了预言中的具体交易地点；保留的时间与售价陈述语法自然。7:17提到城门，但没有保留本句对撒马利亚城门口这一交易地点的明确指定。
  • 2 Kings 7:17–18 · 两细亚大麦要卖一舍客勒银子， — 删除准确移除了大麦的数量与售价这一完整预测。剩余细面陈述仍可自然理解；保留的“也”带有隐含比较，但不使句子不合语法，也不重新表达被删的大麦售价。
  • 2 Kings 7:17–18 · ，一细亚细面也要卖一舍客勒银子 — 删除准确移除了细面的数量与售价预测，留下自然完整的大麦售价陈述。英文明确支持被删的独立商品预测。
  • 2 Samuel 21:15–17 · 非利士人再次与以色列交战， (recoverable from context) — The edit naturally retains David’s response and exhaustion but removes the explicit report that the Philistines again waged war against Israel. The surviving battle narrative makes the conflict inferable, not the full deleted assertion.
  • 2 Samuel 21:15–17 · 大卫和他的臣仆下去迎战非利士人， (recoverable from context) — The remaining sentence is grammatical: 但 introduces David’s exhaustion as a complication during the war. It no longer explicitly reports that David and his servants went down and fought the Philistines. Later references to aid and future battle participation make his involvement inferable without preserving the deleted action statement.
  • 2 Samuel 21:15–17 · ，但大卫疲惫不堪 — The edited verse is a complete, natural report of the renewed war and David’s participation. It omits the separately asserted fact that David became exhausted, which is not explicitly supplied elsewhere in the window.
  • 2 Samuel 21:15–17 · 拉法的后裔伊施比比诺决意杀死大卫。 (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — The deletion removes the attacker’s identity, ancestry, and decision to kill David. The remaining Chinese is grammatically natural, but “他” loses its intended antecedent and may instead be understood as David, potentially transferring the weapon descriptions to him. That reference problem does not negate the supported information loss.
  • 2 Samuel 21:15–17 · 他的铜矛重三百舍客勒， — 删除后不再说明伊施比比诺持有的铜矛及其重量。“身上还佩着一把新剑”可自然承接前句的伊施比比诺，省略主语不造成语法错误；“还”可以作为补充人物信息的表达。

This additional change in the total's apparent scope does not negate the source-supported omission.
  • 2 Samuel 21:20–22 · 每只脚有六根脚趾， (other meaning changed) — The edited verse no longer states that each foot had six toes. The remaining Chinese is grammatical, but “每只手有六根手指，共二十四根” now makes twenty-four appear to be the total number of fingers rather than the combined number of fingers and toes. That additional scope change is separate from the supported information loss.

  • 2 Samuel 21:20–22 · 这四个人都是迦特的拉法后裔， (ambiguous reference) — 删除后只保留集体死亡的陈述，不再明确说明死者是四个人、属于迦特的拉法后裔。“都死在……”是可省略主语的自然汉语结构，但当前窗口此前仅明确叙述一个被杀者，因此“都”所指的群体不再清楚。这是指代问题，不是语法错误。

  • Acts 19:13–16 · 有些四处游走的犹太赶鬼者， (recoverable from context · unit phrase) — 删除了行动者作为四处游走的犹太赶鬼者的明确身份描述。19:14随后说明做这事的是士基瓦的七个儿子，因此完整窗口中零主语可以得到补足；“当时，也试着……”不必判为语法错误，但流动赶鬼者这一身份不再明确陈述。

However, the edited statement no longer identifies the actors as many existing believers or reports their coming forward.   • Judges 18:9–10 · 他们回答说： — The deletion removes the explicit attribution to “they” and the identification of the speech as an answer. The remaining direct quotation is grammatical and continues naturally into 18:10; neither displayed verse supplies the deleted attribution elsewhere.
  • Judges 18:9–10 · ，我们上去攻打他们 — The edited “来吧！” is a natural standalone exhortation. However, the explicit proposal that the speakers join in going up against the people disappears. The surviving instruction to occupy the land does not explicitly state that distinct proposed attack.
  • Judges 18:9–10 · 我们已经看过那地， — The deletion removes the speakers’ completed observation of the land. The remaining “那地非常好” is grammatical and retains their evaluation, but that evaluation does not itself state that they have seen the land.
  • Judges 18:9–10 · ，那地非常好 (recoverable from context) — 删除后只说已经察看那地，不再明确评价那地非常好。余文自然，且是准确删除。18:10仍描述土地宽阔、物产无缺，可以支持这一评价，但没有保留本句的明确判断。
  • Judges 18:9–10 · 你们为什么还不行动？ — 删除了针对听者不行动的直接质问。保留的“不要迟疑，去占领那地吧”仍是行动命令，却没有明确提出听者为何不行动的问题。删除后各句衔接自然，未增添或替换文字。
  • Judges 18:9–10 · 不要迟疑， (recoverable from context) — 删除了明确要求不要迟疑的禁令。前面的质问仍传达催促意味，但不等于明确保留“不许迟疑”这一要求。编辑后的质问接占领命令自然通顺，且仅删除指定文字。
  • Judges 18:9–10 · ，去占领那地吧 — 删除了前往并占领那地的明确命令。此前的攻打提议仍在，但攻打不等于占领。结尾“不要迟疑！”可以自然地承接前面的行动提议，不因省略具体行动而不合语法。
  • Judges 18:9–10 · 你们进去时， (recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the explicit temporal qualification that the encounter occurs when the addressees enter. Entry itself remains stated in “进入一片宽阔的土地,” but its explicit temporal relationship to the encounter does not. The opening “会遇到” naturally inherits its subject from the preceding address to “你们.”
  • Judges 18:9–10 · 会遇到毫无戒备的人民， — The edited verse no longer predicts encountering unsuspecting inhabitants. “你们进去时，进入一片宽阔的土地” is somewhat repetitive, but remains grammatical: the main predicate specifies the kind of land entered, and Chinese does not require an explicit future auxiliary here.
  • Judges 18:9–10 · 进入一片宽阔的土地， (recoverable from context) — The explicit prediction of entering spacious land disappears. Although entry remains in the opening temporal clause and the land remains identifiable from the full window, neither preserves the statement that the destination is spacious. The remaining sentence is grammatical, and “那地” has a clear antecedent in 18:9.
  • Judges 18:9–10 · ，因为上帝已经把那地交在你们手中 — The deletion removes God's completed delivery of the land into the addressees' hands and its role as the reason supporting the prediction. The remaining predictions and description of abundance form fluent sentences. The supplied edit is exactly the indicated deletion.
  • Judges 18:11–13 · 六百名但人带着作战的兵器， (ambiguous reference) — The deletion removes the travelers’ number, Danite identity, and possession of weapons. “于是，从琐拉和以实陶出发。” permits an implicit subject in Chinese, although neither it nor the following “他们” identifies the travelers within this edited window.
  • Judges 18:11–13 · ，从琐拉和以实陶出发 — The edited sentence naturally states that six hundred Danites carried weapons, but no longer states their departure or its places of origin. Subsequent travel does not preserve this specific departure event.
  • Judges 18:11–13 · 他们上去， (recoverable from context) — The upward movement is no longer stated; camping at the destination is a distinct surviving event. The subject of “在犹大的基列耶琳扎营” is naturally recoverable from the six hundred Danites in 18:11, so its omission does not impair grammar.
  • Judges 18:11–13 · ，在犹大的基列耶琳扎营 (other meaning changed) — The edit removes camping at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. The remaining Chinese is grammatical, but “因此” now presents their going up alone as the explanation for the place-name, rather than the original account of going up and camping there. This additional causal shift is nonblocking.
  • Judges 18:11–13 · 基列耶琳以西的那个地方， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed · unit phrase) — 删后可自然省略被命名地点的主语，但不再说明玛哈尼但位于基列耶琳以西。省略也可能使读者误把基列耶琳本身理解为玛哈尼但，而非其西面的地点。
  • Judges 18:11–13 · 他们从那里前往以法莲山地， (recoverable from context) — “来到米迦的家。”可承接上文但人的行动，省略主语并不造成语法问题。不过，从先前地点前往以法莲山地这一行程不再明说；保留到达米迦家的结果并不保留这一独立行程信息。
  • Judges 18:11–13 · ，来到米迦的家 — 删后“他们从那里前往以法莲山地。”语法完整自然，但不再陈述他们来到米迦家的具体到达事件。
  • Judges 18:14–17 · 那五个曾去窥探拉亿地的人对他们的弟兄说： (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the identification of the speakers, their scouting of Laish, and their addressing their brothers. The remaining direct speech is grammatical, although its attribution is no longer explicit. Verse 18:17 partially recovers the five scouts' identity, but not the name Laish or the stated speaker–addressee relationship.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · 这里有一户人家， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The edited statement no longer explicitly locates the objects in a house here. “里面有……” is grammatical with an implicit spatial referent, although the referent is initially less clear. Verse 18:15 supplies the house setting, so contextual recovery does not eliminate the local information loss.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · ，里面有以弗得、家神像、一个雕刻的神像和一个铸造的偶像 (recoverable from context) — The edited speech retains the existence of a house and the instruction to consider what to do, but removes the report identifying the religious objects inside. The supplied punctuation produces grammatical Chinese. Verse 18:17 repeats the objects in the subsequent taking event, making their identity recoverable elsewhere without preserving this explicit report.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · 现在你们想想该怎么做。 — The exact deletion removes the speakers’ instruction to consider what to do. The remaining direct speech is complete and natural.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · 他们就转到那里， (recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the distinct action of turning aside. Arrival and greeting remain. The subject of “来到……向他问安” is recoverable from the preceding narrative, so its omission does not make the Chinese ungrammatical.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · 来到那年轻利未人的住处， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — The edit no longer identifies the destination as the young Levite’s residence. “那里，也就是米迦的家” remains a natural place clarification. However, the surviving “他” loses its explicit Levite antecedent and may now be understood as Micah, potentially changing the recipient of the greeting.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · 也就是米迦的家， — The deletion removes the identification of the young Levite’s residence as Micah’s house. The remaining sequence of turning aside, arriving, and greeting him is grammatical and retains a clear antecedent for “他”.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · ，向他问安 — The exact deletion removes the greeting, a distinct action explicitly supported by the English. The remaining Chinese naturally states their arrival and identifies the house.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · 那六百名但人带着作战的兵器， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — “站在门口。” permits an implicit subject in this narrative context, so it is not ungrammatical. However, the deletion removes the explicit identification of those standing there as six hundred armed Danites. Readers may instead carry forward “他们” from 18:15; 18:17 helps recover the intended armed group.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · ，站在门口 (recoverable from context) — The remaining sentence is grammatical: “带着” functions as the predicate stating that the six hundred Danites carried weapons. Their standing at the gate is no longer stated in this verse, though 18:17 repeats that location and posture.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · 那五个曾去窥探那地的人进去， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes both the entry action and the explicit identification of the takers as the five former scouts. “拿走了……” is grammatical with an implicit subject, but the immediately preceding six hundred Danites could be understood as that subject instead. The five scouts are introduced in 18:14, allowing contextual recovery without eliminating the ambiguity.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · ，拿走了雕刻的神像、以弗得、家神像和铸造的偶像 — The exact deletion leaves two grammatical sentences but removes the distinct action of taking the four cult objects. Their presence in 18:14 does not express their removal.
  • Judges 18:14–17 · 当时祭司正和那六百名带着兵器的人站在门口。 (recoverable from context) — Deleting the complete second sentence leaves a natural, complete account of entry and taking. Although 18:16 preserves the armed men's position at the gate, the edited verse no longer states that the priest stood there with them during the taking.
  • Judges 18:22–23 · 他们离米迦的家已有一段距离时， — 删除后仍是自然完整的叙述，但不再说明但人离开米迦家已有一段距离这一追赶发生时的具体情境。五项检查均通过。
  • Judges 18:22–23 · 米迦家附近各户的人聚集起来， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — 删除明确移除了追赶者的身份和聚集行动。剩余句可采用汉语省略主语的读法，不构成必然的语法错误；但“他们”容易被理解为同时承担离开和追上的动作，使原有两组人物的区分变得含混。18:23的问话可帮助恢复召集人群的情境，却不能恢复附近各户这一身份细节。五项检查均通过，另记录指代及潜在意义变化。
  • Judges 18:22–23 · ，追上了但人 — 删除后句子自然完整，但只叙述附近居民聚集，不再明确叙述他们追上但人的事件。下一节的呼喊和转身不能替代这一明确事件陈述。五项检查均通过。
  • Judges 18:22–23 · 他们在后面呼喊， — 在上一节追上但人的叙述之后，“但人就转过身来”衔接自然；但删除使追赶者在后面呼喊这一动作不再明说。保留转身和问话不等于保留引发回应的呼喊事件。五项检查均通过。
  • Judges 18:22–23 · 但人就转过身来， (other meaning changed) — The exact deletion removes the Danites’ turning to face their pursuers and their explicit identification as speakers. The remaining Chinese is grammatical, but its consecutive predicates naturally make the people calling from behind also the speakers addressing Micah, changing the original speaker attribution.
  • Judges 18:22–23 · 对米迦说： (ambiguous reference) — The quotation can naturally follow the Danites’ action without an explicit speech verb. However, deleting 对米迦说 removes the explicit identification of Micah as the addressee; this is more than removing generic speech framing.
  • Judges 18:22–23 · 你怎么了， — The deletion removes the explicit inquiry about what is wrong with Micah. The remaining 竟召集这么一大群人来？ is a natural incredulous question with an implicit subject supplied by the address to Micah, but it no longer explicitly asks what his trouble is.
  • Judges 18:22–23 · ，竟召集这么一大群人来 (recoverable from context) — The edited question 你怎么了？ is grammatical and natural. It no longer states that Micah assembled such a large company. The preceding verse preserves the surrounding gathering event, but not the deleted question’s explicit attribution of that assembly to Micah or its characterization of the company as large.
  • Judges 18:27–28 · 但人拿走了米迦的神像， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The exact deletion removes the taking of Micah’s idols and Micah’s explicit identification. The remaining sequence is grammatical with an implicit subject, recoverable as the Danites from 18:28. However, “他的祭司” no longer has an explicitly identified possessor in the displayed Chinese window.
  • Judges 18:27–28 · 带走了他的祭司， — The edited verse naturally connects taking the idols with arriving at Laish. It no longer states that the Danites also took Micah’s priest, an independently supported action and participant.
  • Judges 18:27–28 · 来到拉亿， — The edited sequence remains natural and retains arrival among the people, but it no longer identifies their destination as Laish. The surrounding geographical information does not explicitly restore that name.
  • Judges 18:27–28 · 到了那平静而毫无戒备的人民那里， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The edited verse remains grammatical: “他们” can refer implicitly to inhabitants of Laish, especially given the following city's destruction and lack of rescue. However, the explicit introduction of those people and their quiet, unsuspecting condition disappear, leaving the victims less clearly identified.
  • Judges 18:27–28 · 用刀杀了他们， — The exact deletion removes the sword attack on the inhabitants. The remaining Chinese naturally proceeds from arrival to burning the city; burning does not preserve the distinct action of killing its people.
  • Judges 18:27–28 · ，放火烧毁了那城 — The deletion removes the city's destruction by fire. The edited verse ends naturally with the killing of the inhabitants. The subsequent rebuilding does not explicitly retain the burning event.
  • Judges 18:27–28 · 没有人来救他们， (possible other meaning changed) — The absence of anyone to rescue the inhabitants is no longer stated. In the full window, the opening 因为 clause can naturally function as a postposed explanation of the preceding account of the attack and destruction, without an obligatory 所以. This may shift the stated causal connection from the absence of rescue to the attack's outcome.
  • Judges 18:27–28 · 因为那城离西顿很远， (possible other meaning changed) — The city's distance from Sidon and its explicit role as a reason for the lack of rescue disappear. The remaining 也没有与任何人结盟 permits an implicit city/community subject recoverable from the surrounding narrative. Removing 因为 also makes the surviving lack of alliances a juxtaposed fact rather than an explicitly marked cause.
  • Judges 18:27–28 · 也没有与任何人结盟； (possible other meaning changed) — 删除后不再说明该城没有与任何人结盟，也失去了无人救援的一个明确原因。剩余中文语法成立，且为精确删除。不过，原来用分号分开的山谷位置说明现在接在“因为”句后，可能被读成无人救援的另一个原因。
  • Judges 18:27–28 · ；那城位于伯利合附近的山谷中 — 精确删除了该城位于伯利合附近山谷中的地点说明。删除后，无人救援及其原因直接衔接但人的重建和居住行为，中文自然，其他事件含义保持。
  • Judges 18:27–28 · 但人重建了那城， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — 精确删除了但人重建该城的事件。剩下的“住在那里。”可以作为中文省略主语的陈述，18:27已经引入但人，因此不能仅因主语省略判为不合语法。不过，中间插入了关于居民和城址的叙述，居住者的指向变得不够明确。主体可由上下文恢复，不代表重建行为仍被表达。
  • Judges 18:27–28 · ，住在那里 — 精确删除了但人在该城居住的行动。剩余“但人重建了那城。”完整自然；重建并不必然表示重建者随后住在那里，因此居住信息确实消失。
  • Judges 18:29–31 · 他们按着祖先但的名字， (unit phrase) — The edit removes the explanation that the city was named after their ancestor Dan. The remaining naming statement permits an implicit subject in Chinese, with the Danites identifiable from the window.
  • Judges 18:29–31 · 但原是以色列所生的儿子； — The edit cleanly removes Dan’s relationship to Israel while retaining grammatical statements about the city’s new and former names.
  • Judges 18:29–31 · ；那城从前名叫拉亿 — The edit removes the city’s former name, Laish. The remaining naming and parentage statements are complete and natural.
  • Judges 18:29–31 · 但人为自己设立了偶像。 (recoverable from context) — 删除了但人为自己设立偶像这一明确行动。剩余祭司任职句完整自然。18:31再次提到设立神像，使该行动可从上下文恢复，但不改变它已从18:30的陈述中消失这一事实。
  • Judges 18:29–31 · 以及约拿单的子孙， (possible other meaning changed · unit phrase) — 删除了约拿单的子孙也担任祭司这一参与者信息。剩余句以约拿单为主语，语法自然。不过任职至被掳之日的时间限定现在仅落在约拿单本人身上，而原文涉及他及其子孙，可能额外改变任职期限的解读。
  • Judges 18:29–31 · ，直到那地的居民被掳的日子 (unit phrase) — The exact deletion leaves a grammatical statement of priestly service but removes its stated endpoint: the captivity of the land's inhabitants.
  • Judges 18:29–31 · 上帝的殿在示罗的整个时期， (unit phrase) — The remaining Chinese naturally states that the image remained there, but no longer identifies the period by the presence of God's house in Shiloh.
  • Judges 18:29–31 · 但人为自己设立的米迦所雕刻的神像， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context · unit phrase) — Chinese permits an implicit subject for 一直都在那里, and the idols in 18:30 provide a possible antecedent. However, the explicit identification as Micah's carved image and the statement that the Danites set it up for themselves disappear. The implicit subject is less secure and could instead be understood as God's house or another preceding referent.
  • Judges 9:1–2 · 耶路巴力的儿子亚比米勒来到示剑， (ambiguous reference) — The deletion removes the visitor’s name, parentage, and arrival at Shechem. The remaining coordinated predicates permit an implicit subject in Chinese, although this window no longer identifies the person referred to by 他.
  • Judges 9:1–2 · 去见他母亲的兄弟们， (ambiguous reference) — The visit to his mother’s brothers and their explicit identification disappear. 对他们和他母亲的全族说 remains grammatical, but 他们 no longer has an explicit antecedent in the displayed window.
  • Judges 9:1–2 · 对他们和他母亲的全族说： (recoverable from context) — The following direct quotation still conveys Abimelech’s speech, and Chinese permits its juxtaposition with the preceding action narration. However, the statement that he addresses his mother’s entire clan, in addition to her brothers, is no longer explicit.
  • Judges 9:1–2 · 请你们问示剑所有的首领： (other meaning changed) — The edited speech remains intelligible and grammatical as a quoted rhetorical question followed by a reminder; the nested quotation marks do not require a missing grammatical complement. It no longer instructs the relatives to question all Shechem’s leaders. The question now reads as presented directly to the current audience rather than explicitly designated for relay.
  • Judges 9:1–2 · 是让耶路巴力的七十个儿子全都统治你们好， (other meaning changed) — The deletion removes the proposed rule by all seventy sons of Jerubbaal. The remaining question is grammatical: “还是让一个人统治你们好？” can ask whether one-person rule would be preferable. However, 还是 now suggests a preference rather than explicitly introducing the second option of the original two-option question.
  • Judges 9:1–2 · ，还是让一个人统治你们好 (other meaning changed) — The one-man alternative is deleted. The remaining “是让耶路巴力的七十个儿子全都统治你们好？” can function as an intonational confirmation question about whether that arrangement is good; Chinese does not require 吗 in every such question. It no longer explicitly asks the audience to choose between two arrangements.
  • Judges 9:1–2 · 要记得， — The edited verse retains the kinship assertion but removes the explicit instruction to remember it. “我是你们的骨肉” is a natural independent statement. Here 要记得 is an imperative directing the listeners to keep a specific relationship in mind, not merely an intensifier of that relationship.
  • Judges 9:1–2 · ，我是你们的骨肉 (possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — The explicit kinship claim disappears. The final “要记得。” is grammatical as an imperative with an implicit object, although it may now refer to the preceding question or instruction rather than to kinship. The family setting in 9:1 makes the relationship partly recoverable but does not preserve its explicit assertion in the edited verse.
  • Judges 9:7–8 · 有人把这事告诉约坦， (ambiguous reference) — The deletion removes the report to Jotham and his explicit identification. The remaining Chinese is grammatical, although “他” has no identified antecedent within the displayed window.
  • Judges 9:7–8 · 他就登上基利心山顶， (possible other meaning changed) — The ascent to the summit disappears. The remaining sentence is grammatical, but its default subject continuity can make the person reporting the matter, rather than Jotham, the person shouting.
  • Judges 9:7–8 · 示剑的首领们啊， (ambiguous reference · unit phrase) — The address remains natural, but it no longer identifies the audience as the leaders of Shechem. The surviving “你们” refers to an unspecified audience within this window.
  • Judges 9:7–8 · 请听我说， — The deletion removes Jotham’s explicit request that the leaders listen to him. The address and wish that God hear them remain grammatical; the surviving 也 does not make the sentence ungrammatical.
  • Judges 9:7–8 · ，愿上帝也听你们 — The edited verse naturally ends with the request to listen. It no longer expresses Jotham’s wish that God hear the leaders.
  • Judges 9:7–8 · 树木出去， (ambiguous reference) — The deletion removes both the identification of the actors as trees and their setting-out action. The purpose of appointing a king and the subsequent request remain. Chinese permits an implicit subject in 要膏立一位王来统治自己, but the surviving 它们 no longer has an explicit antecedent identifying that group.
  • Judges 9:7–8 · ，要膏立一位王来统治自己 (recoverable from context) — The exact deletion leaves grammatical Chinese but removes the stated purpose of going out: anointing a king to rule the trees. The subsequent request still suggests their desire for a king, but does not explicitly state the intention to anoint one.
  • Judges 9:7–8 · 它们对橄榄树说： (recoverable from context) — The standalone direct quotation can naturally follow the narrative without an explicit speech introduction. The trees remain inferable as its speakers, but the olive tree is no longer identified as the recipient of their request.
  • Judges 9:9–10 · 橄榄树却回答： (ambiguous reference) — The remaining direct question is grammatical, but the displayed window no longer explicitly identifies the olive tree as its speaker or presents it as a reply. Oil production may suggest the speaker, but does not explicitly name it.
  • Judges 9:9–10 · 难道我要停止出产那使上帝和人都得尊荣的油， (other meaning changed) — “去统治众树吗？” is a natural elliptical question with its speaker supplied by the attribution. The deletion removes oil production, its honoring of God and man, and the proposed sacrifice of that production. It also changes a rhetorical objection into a more open question about ruling.
  • Judges 9:9–10 · ，去统治众树吗 (other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — The remaining “难道我要停止出产……的油？” is a complete, natural rhetorical question; “吗” is not required. The proposed purpose of ruling the trees disappears. The subsequent invitation to the fig tree preserves the kingship theme, but not this explicit alternative for the olive tree. The edited objection concerns stopping production generally rather than stopping it to rule.
  • Judges 9:13–14 · 葡萄树却回答： (ambiguous reference) — The remaining direct question is grammatical, but the displayed window no longer identifies its speaker as the grapevine or explicitly presents it as a reply.
  • Judges 9:13–14 · 难道我要停止出产那使上帝和人都欢喜的酒， (possible other meaning changed) — “去统治众树吗？” is a natural elliptical question with the grapevine retained as speaker. It omits the contemplated sacrifice of wine production and the wine's beneficiaries. Without 难道 and the stated sacrifice, it can also sound more like a neutral question than a rhetorical refusal.
  • Judges 9:13–14 · ，去统治众树吗 — The remaining 难道 question is grammatical without 吗. It retains the contemplated cessation of wine production but removes ruling the trees as the proposed alternative and purpose.
  • Judges 9:13–14 · 所有的树木都对荆棘说： (ambiguous reference) — The result can function as a final, unattributed direct utterance; the quotation itself is a natural request. However, neither its collective speakers nor its recipient is explicitly identified, leaving an ambiguous transition after the grapevine's speech.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · 荆棘回答： (ambiguous reference) — The deletion removes the explicit identification of the thornbush as the responding speaker. The remaining direct speech is grammatical, but its first-person speaker is no longer explicitly identified in the displayed Chinese window.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · 你们若真心膏立我作你们的王， (other meaning changed) — The genuine anointing of the speaker as king is no longer stated as the condition for seeking refuge. 就来躲在我的荫下 can naturally function as an imperative. The surviving 不然 now most naturally refers to refusing that invitation rather than failing the original anointing condition.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · 不然， (other meaning changed · unit word) — 不然 explicitly restricts the curse to the failure of the preceding condition. Removing it leaves grammatical Chinese but no longer states that restriction; the curse can now read as an independent wish rather than the alternative to genuine anointing.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · 愿火从荆棘中出来， (other meaning changed) — The deletion removes the wish for fire to emerge from the thornbush, a distinct event not preserved by the remaining burning outcome. The remaining Chinese is grammatical as an imperative, but consequently changes a curse into an apparent instruction to burn the cedars.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · ，烧灭黎巴嫩的香柏树 — The edited curse naturally ends with fire coming out of the thornbush. It no longer states that this fire consumes Lebanon's cedars.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · 你们立亚比米勒为王， (ambiguous reference) — The audience's appointment of Abimelech as king is no longer stated. The conditional chain remains grammatical with implicit subjects and an implicit action under evaluation; its unfinished structure already exists in the original window. However, 若是出于忠诚和正直 now leaves the relevant action unspecified.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · 若是出于忠诚和正直， — The edit removes the substantive condition that making Abimelech king was done faithfully and honestly. The remaining parallel conditional clauses are grammatical within the displayed, continuing sentence. The supplied edit is exactly the stated deletion.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · 若是善待耶路巴力和他的家， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — The condition of treating Jerubbaal and his family well disappears. The remaining Chinese is grammatical, but 他 in 若是照他应得的报答他 loses its explicit Jerubbaal antecedent and could instead be read as referring to Abimelech. This referential risk does not negate the supported omission.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · 若是照他应得的报答他—— — The edit removes the explicit condition that Jerubbaal receive treatment corresponding to what he deserves. General good treatment remains but does not express that standard of recompense. The final comma can connect naturally to the explanatory 因为 clause in 9:17; the continuing conditional structure is already present in the source window.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · 因为我父亲曾为你们争战， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the father's fighting on the audience's behalf, his explicit relationship to the speaker, and the explicit causal link. Risking his life and delivering the audience remain; these do not preserve the distinct fighting action. After the preceding dash, the remaining clause can naturally have an implicit subject referring back to Jerubbaal, although that subject is less explicit.
  • Judges 9:15–17 · 冒着生命危险救你们脱离米甸人的手； — 删除后只说明父亲曾为听众争战，不再明确说明他冒生命危险、救他们脱离米甸人的手。剩余的“因为我父亲曾为你们争战，”在前节破折号引出的解释中仍自然可读；末尾逗号不造成内部语法结构残缺。编辑也确实仅删除指定文本。
  • Judges 9:21–25 · 约坦逃到比珥， (ambiguous reference) — The deletion removes Jotham's identification and his escape to Beer. The remaining Chinese permits an implicit subject and is grammatical, but neither the subject of 住 nor the location referred to by 那里 is identified in the remaining window.
  • Judges 9:21–25 · 因为惧怕他的兄弟亚比米勒， — The edited verse naturally states Jotham's escape and subsequent residence but no longer states his fear of Abimelech or their brotherhood.
  • Judges 9:21–25 · ，就住在那里 (possible other meaning changed) — The edited sentence is grammatical and retains the escape to Beer and fear of Abimelech, but removes Jotham's subsequent residence. The remaining causal phrase now modifies the escape directly, whereas the English explicitly connects the fear with his residence.
  • Judges 9:21–25 · 上帝使一个引起仇恨的灵介入亚比米勒和示剑首领之间， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — The remaining causative clause can grammatically follow the temporal clause in 9:22 and the purpose clause in 9:24. However, God is no longer identified as its subject, and the intervention of the spirit disappears. The preceding mention of Abimelech may now invite an unintended reading in which he causes the leaders' deceit.
  • Judges 9:21–25 · 使示剑的首领以诡诈待亚比米勒， — The edit removes God's causing the leaders to treat Abimelech deceitfully. Sending a spirit of animosity does not itself explicitly state that distinct action. The remaining sentence connects naturally to the purpose clause in 9:24.
  • Judges 9:21–25 · 为要追讨杀害耶路巴力七十个儿子的罪， (ambiguous reference · possible other meaning changed) — The deletion removes the explicit purpose of bringing the murder of Jerubbaal's seventy sons to justice, including their identity and number. The remaining causative clause connects grammatically to 9:23, but '他们的兄弟' loses its intended antecedent and may now be read as referring to the leaders of Shechem.
  • Judges 9:21–25 · 使他们的兄弟亚比米勒和帮助他杀害兄弟的示剑首领， (ambiguous reference · other meaning changed · unit phrase) — The edit removes the explicit identification of Abimelech and the assisting leaders as the joint bearers of bloodguilt, together with the leaders' role in helping murder his brothers. In the full window, '都承担' can take the previously mentioned plural leaders as its implicit subject, so it is grammatically possible. That reading, however, no longer expressly includes Abimelech among those bearing guilt.
  • Judges 9:21–25 · 示剑的首领在山顶设下埋伏， (possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the leaders' setting an ambush on the hilltops. The remaining “要对付亚比米勒；他们抢劫……” is grammatical with the Shechem leaders recoverable from the preceding context. However, the intention to oppose Abimelech is now detached from the ambush and may instead be understood as motivating the robbery.
  • Judges 9:21–25 · 要对付亚比米勒； — The edited verse naturally joins the ambush and robbery clauses. It no longer explicitly identifies Abimelech as the intended target of the ambush; his remaining role as recipient of the report does not preserve that relationship.
  • Judges 9:21–25 · ；他们抢劫所有从那条路经过的人 (possible other meaning changed) — The robbery of passing travelers disappears, while the ambush and report remain in grammatical sentences. The remaining “这事” now refers naturally to the ambush alone, potentially narrowing the reported matter compared with the original.
  • Judges 9:21–25 · 有人把这事告诉了亚比米勒。 — Deleting the final sentence leaves a complete, natural account of the ambush and robbery. It removes the separate event of someone informing Abimelech, which is explicitly supported by the English.
  • Judges 9:30–33 · ，就怒火中烧 — The edited verse naturally states that Zebul heard Gaal’s words, but no longer states his angry reaction. His subsequent covert message does not explicitly preserve that reaction.
  • Judges 9:30–33 · 他暗中派使者去见亚比米勒， (possible other meaning changed) — The preceding verse supplies Zebul as the natural implicit subject of “说”, so the edited passage remains grammatical. It loses the covert dispatch of messengers and the identification of Abimelech as recipient. Retaining “说” alone can also suggest Zebul speaks directly rather than communicating through messengers.
  • Judges 9:30–33 · 以别的儿子迦勒和他的兄弟们来到示剑， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — Accepted: the deletion removes the arrival in Shechem and the explicit identification of Gaal and his brothers as the actors. “看哪，正在煽动全城反叛你” permits an implicit subject in this window, where Gaal is already salient, although the precise group responsible becomes less explicit.
  • Judges 9:30–33 · ，正在煽动全城反叛你 — Accepted: the edited report naturally states only that Gaal and his brothers have arrived in Shechem. Their distinct action of inciting the city against Abimelech is no longer stated.
  • Judges 9:30–33 · 你和跟随你的人要在今晚前来， (possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the instruction for Abimelech and his followers to come tonight. “现在，埋伏在田间。” is a grammatical imperative with an implicit addressee recoverable from 9:31. However, “现在” can now suggest immediate execution rather than introducing instructions for tonight.
  • Judges 9:30–33 · ，埋伏在田间 — The edited verse naturally instructs Abimelech and his followers to come tonight, but no longer instructs them to lie in wait or identifies the fields as their ambush location.
  • Judges 9:30–33 · 明早太阳一出来， — The instruction to rise and attack remains grammatical after the preceding instruction to come and ambush. The explicit next-morning sunrise timing is no longer stated; “就” can connect the instruction to the preceding discourse without requiring the removed temporal clause.
  • Judges 9:30–33 · 你就起来攻城。 (other meaning changed) — The instruction to rise and attack the city disappears. The remaining sentence is grammatical: its initial sunrise expression and following encounter condition introduce the instruction to deal with Gaal's men. The deletion also shifts the explicit sunrise timing from the city attack to the remaining encounter/response instruction.
  • Judges 9:30–33 · 迦勒和他的人出来迎战时， (possible other meaning changed · recoverable from context) — 删除了迦勒及其部众出城迎战这一预期事件，以及以该事件为行动时机的条件。余句语法完整；“他们”可由9:31的迦勒及其兄弟们恢复理解。原文要求在敌人出战时对付他们，删后可能被理解为攻城时直接对付他们，不再受原有时机限制。
  • Judges 9:36–37 · 迦勒看见那些人， (recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the explicit event of Gaal seeing the people and his explicit identification as the initial speaker. The remaining implicit-subject speech clause is acceptable Chinese; “迦勒又说” in 9:37 helps recover the speaker. The surviving report does not explicitly state the separate perception event.
  • Judges 9:36–37 · 就对西布勒说： (recoverable from context) — The quotation still conveys Gaal's speech, but the statement no longer explicitly identifies Zebul as its addressee. Zebul's subsequent reply makes that relationship recoverable. An action clause followed directly by a quotation is acceptable Chinese narrative ellipsis, so the absence of a speech verb does not itself make this result ungrammatical.
  • Judges 9:36–37 · ，有人从山上下来了 — The edited “看哪！” is a natural standalone exclamation, but it no longer reports people descending from the mountains. Zebul's reference to mountain shadows and Gaal's later report of movement from other locations do not explicitly preserve that particular report.
  • Judges 9:36–37 · 西布勒却回答： (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the explicit identification of Zebul as the speaker replying to Gaal. The adjacent quotations remain readable as dialogue, although the second speaker must now be inferred. This is not merely redundant speech framing because attribution no longer remains explicit.
  • Judges 9:36–37 · 迦勒又说： (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The quotation remains grammatical as an untagged dialogue turn following 9:36. Nevertheless, the explicit identification of Gaal as speaking again is lost; dialogue sequence and content only allow the reader to infer it.
  • Judges 9:36–37 · 有人从那地的中央下来， — 删除后不再明确陈述有人从那地的中央下来。剩余的“还有一队”可自然承接9:36已经提到的人，整句通顺；保留的橡树路线并未表达被删的人群动向。
  • Judges 9:36–37 · ，还有一队从占卜者橡树那条路过来 — 删除后只保留有人从那地的中央下来的报告，不再陈述另有一队经占卜者橡树路线而来。所给编辑结果是原句的直接删除，语法完整，且该信息损失有英文明确支持。
  • Judges 9:42–45 · 第二天， (unit phrase) — The exact deletion leaves a natural Chinese sentence but removes the explicit timing of the outing and report. “第二天” specifies a subsequent day, rather than merely marking discourse progression.
  • Judges 9:42–45 · 示剑的百姓出到田间， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes the explicit event being reported, including the identification of the people as those of Shechem. “第二天，有人把这事告诉了亚比米勒。” is grammatical, although “这事” lacks its original explicit antecedent. The subsequent account helps readers infer the outing but does not explicitly restore all the deleted information.
  • Judges 9:42–45 · ，有人把这事告诉了亚比米勒 — The edited verse is a complete, natural sentence. It retains the people's outing but deletes the separate event of someone reporting it to Abimelech. His subsequent military response does not preserve that reporting event.
  • Judges 9:42–45 · 他就带着自己的人， (recoverable from context) — The deletion removes Abimelech's taking his men with him. “分作三队，埋伏在田间。” permits an implicit military participant in this narrative: Abimelech is already named, and 9:44 explicitly supplies his companies. The resulting division and ambush do not themselves state the distinct action of taking his men.
  • Judges 9:42–45 · 分作三队， (recoverable from context) — The exact deletion removes the action of dividing his men into three companies. The remaining Chinese naturally says that he took his men and lay in ambush. The later reference to the other two companies helps recover the organization, but does not preserve the explicit division event in this statement.
  • Judges 9:42–45 · ，埋伏在田间 — The exact deletion removes the ambush action and its location. “他就带着自己的人，分作三队” remains grammatical, and the next sentence naturally continues with his observation of the people.
  • Judges 9:42–45 · 他看见百姓从城里出来， (ambiguous reference · recoverable from context) — The deletion removes his seeing the people come out of the city and the explicit timing of the attack relative to that observation. “就起来攻击他们” can grammatically continue with an implicit subject across the sentence boundary. Its object “他们” has a less immediate antecedent after deletion, but the people in 9:42 and the attack in 9:44 support the intended reference.
